title: Repeated String Match
summary: Determine the least number of repetitions of string a required for string b to become a substring.
statement: Determine the least number of repetitions of string a required for string b to become a substring. If b cannot be a substring of any repetition of a, return -1. Repetition of an empty string a zero times results in an empty string, one repetition yields a, and two repetitions yield aa.
constraints: Return the fewest repetitions of a whose concatenation contains b, or -1.
reference_solution:
def repeated_string_count(a, b):
    count=(len(b)+len(a)-1)//len(a)
    text=a*count
    if b in text:return count
    if b in text+a:return count+1
    return -1

hints: A target match can begin near the end of one copy and finish in the next.
Build the ceiling number of copies, then test it and exactly one additional copy.
q=ceil(len(b)/len(a)); check a*q, then a*(q+1), else -1.
Any longer target needs enough copies for its length, and a start offset shorter than one base copy requires at most one extra copy.
